title: session/set-config-option
description: Request `session/set-config-option` (client -> daemon): set one of the session configuration options the AGENT announced when the session opened, over the live ACP connection (`session/set_config_option`), without relaunching the session. The options themselves are never listed by a verb: the agent announces them at the handshake and the daemon records them as a `config_options_announced` event on the session log, the same place the handshake's other facts land. A surface therefore offers the live change exactly where that event exists — an agent that announced nothing gets no selector invented in its name. Refused with CONFIG_OPTION_NOT_ANNOUNCED (2007) for an unknown option id, a value the option does not list, or a session whose agent announced nothing.

configValue.description: One selectable value of a `select` option, as the agent announced it.

id.description: The value's identifier — what is sent back to choose it.

name.description: Human-readable label the agent gave it.

description.description: The agent's own description, when it sent one.

configOption.description: One session configuration option, relayed verbatim from the agent. Meltemi adds no entry of its own: an embedded catalog of models would be the core assuming a provider and would rot silently with every model released.

id.description: The option's identifier — what is sent back to set it.

name.description: Human-readable label the agent gave it.

description.description: The agent's own description, when it sent one.

category.description: The ACP category verbatim (`model`, `mode`, `modelConfig`, `thoughtLevel`, or anything else the agent sent). A free string and not an enum because ACP leaves the space open and requires clients to handle categories they do not know; a closed enum would turn the next category the spec adds into a parse failure.

type.description: The option's shape, mirroring ACP's own two kinds. It is what decides how a chosen value is read.

currentValue.description: The value in force right now: a value id for `select`, a boolean for `boolean`.

values.description: Everything the agent said can be chosen. Present for `select` only.

sessionId.description: The live session whose option to set.

optionId.description: The option's id, as the agent announced it.

value.description: The chosen value: for a select, the id of one of the announced values; for a boolean, `true` or `false`. One string, and which of the two it means is decided by the kind the AGENT announced for this option — never by the caller and never by a guess. The daemon checks the value against that declaration and refuses what it does not match, so a select that happens to list a value called `true` is still resolved as a select.

options.description: The options as the AGENT reports them after the change — its answer, not our projection of what we asked for. An agent that clamps, renames or reorders is reported as it actually is.
